what: The independent reader's flags on the GitLab relocation translation with one planted mistake (tour stop 9). Copied from its recorded run: the reader is an AI model (Claude Opus 5.5) given only the policy's text, a short brief and the translation's files, asked to flag every place where the translation departs from the policy. It was not told that a mistake was planted, or where.

flags.source: U6: 'must reside in their primary location for at least 183 days ... may live or work outside their permanent location ... for a maximum total of 183 days'
flags.translation: _days: Eq(sn_s, sg_s) with sg_s = elapsed_days(sf_s, sl_s), i.e. a stay's days = last day minus first day (R1)
flags.why: A stay from 1 Jan to 1 Jan, which is one day away, counts as 0 days, so every stay is undercounted by one day. That pushes 'out' down and 'inn' up and can give a definite resok/outok/workok YES (and ltr/comp NO) when the person has actually gone over 183 days outside. The separate sg/sn bases and R3's '-1' both fit inclusive counting (sn = sg + 1), so the rule is also inconsistent with the rest of the translation.

flags.source: U6: 'If you believe you may exceed ... the 183 days limit (or a lower threshold in certain countries)'
flags.translation: _residence: B = out <= 183 applied to every place
flags.why: The source says some countries have a lower threshold. A stay under 183 days in such a country still gets a definite resok/workok YES.

flags.source: U15: 'If you plan on staying in a location for more than 6 months in a single calendar year ... you must complete the long-term relocation process'
flags.translation: _days: pd_pl = sum of the place's actual stays only, but it is defined (as 0 for a plan-only place) whenever the place has a plan child; _longterm/_shortterm then apply the NO conditions (pd <= 181, not chg, not mail)
flags.why: A planned stay's length is never counted. A place with only a planned stay, or a planned stay on top of short actual stays, gets a definite ltr/mustltr NO and st YES even when the person plans to stay more than 6 months, which the source says must go through the long-term process.

flags.source: U16: 'team members cannot take company-owned devices to or otherwise work from US-embargoed countries ... some places are subject to trade control restrictions'; U17: 'Additional information can be found on the Trade Compliance page'
flags.translation: _device: devok YES when And(Not emb, notice met, approval met) (R5)
flags.why: The source only prohibits devices in embargoed places and points to other trade-control restrictions outside the pinned text. A definite device permission elsewhere is an inference the text does not make. The embargo NO and the list in _embargo are faithful.
